raw_response:
I'm 67 this year, been farming this land since I was 22. My old man passed ten years ago, but my sons and daughter-in-law still help when they can — though two of them work in the county factory and only come back for the busy weeks. I didn't finish school, just a few years of primary, but I know this soil better than any book. We've got 6 mu, not much, but it's ours. I don't try fancy things. At my age, change is risk.

**How I'll manage this year**

The garlic went in last October on 3 mu, same as always. I saved the big cloves from the previous harvest for seed, bought a little to top up what was too small. It's greening up nice now. Old Zhang next door — his garlic always looks good — he says the winter was mild so we should watch for disease. I'll irrigate twice more before harvest: once when the weather warms proper, and again when the bulbs start swelling in May. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu already in March, about 50 kg each. If the leaves look yellow before harvest, I'll throw on another half-bag of urea, but probably not — last year was fine without it. The garlic needs hand-weeding, lots of bending work. My daughter-in-law and my youngest son do most of that now, my knees can't take it. I expect around 1,200 jin per mu if the rain cooperates, same as last year. I'll spray a fungicide once if I see white spots on the leaves — happened two years ago, lost money.

The wheat is on the other 3 mu. I keep that for our own flour, can't buy everything. It's at green-up now. Every year at Qingming I topdress with urea — about 20 kg per mu — and water it right after. That's the most important thing. Maybe water again at heading if May is dry. I don't spray much on wheat, only if I see aphids. Should get 400-450 kg per mu, enough for the family and a little to sell. My eldest son has a friend with a combine, so harvest is easier than it used to be.

Now the maize — that's after the garlic comes out in late May and the wheat in mid-June. We'll plant maize on all 6 mu. The garlic land has more time, so that's fine. The wheat land is tight — sometimes less than a week between harvest and planting. When that happens, we hire Old Li's tractor to plow fast, costs money but you can't miss the window. I buy hybrid seed from the supply shop, about 3 kg per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting — one bag per mu, about 50 kg. Then when the maize is knee-high, I topdress with urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. Irrigate once or twice in summer, depends on the rains. If July is wet, maybe not at all. I spray herbicide right after planting, saves a lot of hoeing later. Yield should be around 450-500 kg per mu. My neighbor's son bought a maize harvest machine last year, so I pay him to do the cutting now — my back can't handle that anymore.

**Money and tradeoffs**

Everything costs. Seed, fertilizer, diesel for the pump, hiring the tractor and harvester. I figure maybe 4,000-5,000 yuan total for inputs this year. My second son sends 1,000 yuan a month from his job in Shijiazhuang, which is how we afford the fertilizer upfront. Without that, I'd have to cut back. I thought about planting more garlic since prices were decent last year, but it's too much work for an old woman. And if the price drops, you lose more. So I keep the same rotation. Better to be steady than sorry.
